rv.q: It’s a great hodgepodge of vampire tropes, some of which work better than others under Hunter Bird's direction — such as a great bit of staging where Valerie and her vampire companions admire themselves in a mirror and see no reflections, only their clothes. However, none of the themes feel fully fleshed out enough for an emotional payoff.
Blood/Love subtitled “A Vampire Pop Opera” is an exciting production which can rival the rock operas of the past in energy and passion.
Blood/Love could be the silly, sensual distraction you need right now.
But I notice that I start cringing every time I see that facial expression because that’s about all we get from her.

cn.t: This vampire pop opera wins critics over with high-energy performances and self-aware camp, though some find the story forgettable. Most agree it's slick, fun entertainment that doesn't take itself too seriously.
